comment: Declared intent: which model artifacts MailWeave's semantic rung may use, from which
host, under which licence, and how large each set is allowed to be. Reviewed by a human.
An entry has one or more ARTIFACT SETS rather than a file list, because a repo ships
the same weights in several formats and a runtime needs exactly one of them.
BAAI/bge-reranker-base carries model.safetensors AND pytorch_model.bin AND
onnx/model.onnx: downloading the repo is about 3.36 GB for roughly 1.1 GB of weights
anyone uses. A set names the format its runtime loads, so the Python arm and PF-4b's
ONNX arm are locked separately and stay separately identifiable.
Patterns are fnmatch over the repo-relative path. Every `required` pattern must match at
least one file at pin time or the pin fails: a pattern that silently matches nothing is
how a tokenizer goes missing and the failure surfaces later as a model-quality result.
This file pins nothing. Revisions and digests arrive from a real download via
`mailweave setup-models --pin` and land in models.lock, which is then reviewed.

stage_a_default.why: AD D.5's default stage A: 32.3M params, MIT, ungated. Chosen over EmbeddingGemma because that one is HF-gated, which is friction against NFR-04's clean-machine setup.

python-st.why: modules.json is REQUIRED, not optional: at revision 6fc8051 it declares sentence_transformers.models.StaticEmbedding and Normalize, and without it SentenceTransformer falls back to a transformer-style load this repo cannot satisfy. A missing modules.json would present as a loader failure and get read as a model problem.

stage_b_default.why: AD D.5's default stage B, scored over the shortlist only: cross-encoders have no reusable per-document work, so their cost is linear in pool size and affordable only over max_rerank_pairs candidates.

python-st.why: the CrossEncoder path: safetensors weights plus the tokenizer and config it loads. pytorch_model.bin and onnx/model.onnx are the same weights twice over and are excluded rather than downloaded and ignored.

node-onnx.why: PF-4b's arm. Locked separately so the Node measurement is known to be against ONNX artifacts and the Python measurement against safetensors, rather than both citing 'bge-reranker-base' and differing for a reason nobody recorded.

stage_a_swap.why: AD D.5's opt-in swap, behind the same SEM-03 interface. Present so that 'a second implementation registers without touching retrieval logic' is a claim something can exercise. Not pinned by default: it is the alternate, not the default.

python-st.why: same shape as the default's set; the gguf variants are a different runtime entirely and are excluded rather than pulled.
